_note: A starter set of well-known people and places, written by hand so the reader has something real to mark while the full dataset is sorted out. It is deliberately small and covers the figures and locations most readers meet first. Matching is by surname-free exact word, so only unambiguous names are listed: 'John' and 'Mary' are left out because each names several different people and marking them all alike would be wrong. Replacing this file with a full dataset needs no change to the reader.
_source: General reference. Meanings of Hebrew and Greek names follow the usual lexical sources; where a meaning is disputed it is left out rather than guessed.

people.name: Abram
people.note: Called out of Haran to a land God would show him. Renamed Abraham, father of a multitude, in Genesis 17:5.

people.name: Abraham
people.note: The patriarch God covenanted with. Father of Isaac.

people.name: Sarai
people.note: Wife of Abram. Renamed Sarah in Genesis 17:15.

people.name: Sarah
people.note: Wife of Abraham, mother of Isaac.

people.name: Isaac
people.note: Son of Abraham and Sarah, father of Jacob and Esau.

people.name: Rebekah
people.note: Wife of Isaac, mother of Jacob and Esau.

people.name: Jacob
people.meaning: Supplanter, or one who takes by the heel
people.note: Son of Isaac. Renamed Israel in Genesis 32:28. Father of the twelve tribes.

people.name: Esau
people.note: Jacob's elder twin, who sold his birthright.

people.name: Rachel
people.note: Jacob's wife, mother of Joseph and Benjamin.

people.name: Leah
people.note: Jacob's first wife, mother of six of the tribes.

people.name: Lot
people.note: Abram's nephew, who settled near Sodom.

people.name: Noah
people.note: Built the ark and survived the flood.

people.name: Adam
people.note: The first man.

people.name: Eve
people.note: The first woman, called the mother of all living.

people.name: Cain
people.note: Adam's firstborn, who killed his brother Abel.

people.name: Abel
people.note: Adam's second son, killed by Cain.

people.name: Enoch
people.note: Walked with God and was taken, rather than dying.

people.name: Methuselah
people.note: The longest-lived man recorded in Scripture.

people.name: Melchizedek
people.note: Priest-king of Salem who blessed Abram.

people.name: Ishmael
people.note: Son of Abram and Hagar.

people.name: Hagar
people.note: Sarai's Egyptian servant, mother of Ishmael.

people.name: Moses
people.note: Led Israel out of Egypt and received the law at Sinai.

people.name: Aaron
people.note: Moses' brother and Israel's first high priest.

people.name: Miriam
people.note: Sister of Moses and Aaron, a prophetess.

people.name: Joshua
people.note: Succeeded Moses and led Israel into Canaan.

people.name: Caleb
people.note: One of the two spies who urged Israel to take the land.

people.name: Pharaoh
people.note: The title of Egypt's king, used in Scripture as a name.

people.name: Gideon
people.note: A judge who defeated Midian with three hundred men.

people.name: Samson
people.note: A judge of extraordinary strength, undone by Delilah.

people.name: Delilah
people.note: The woman who drew out the secret of Samson's strength.

people.name: Ruth
people.note: A Moabitess who stayed with Naomi and became David's great-grandmother.

people.name: Naomi
people.note: Ruth's mother-in-law, who returned to Bethlehem.

people.name: Boaz
people.note: Ruth's kinsman-redeemer and husband.

people.name: Samuel
people.note: Prophet who anointed both Saul and David.

people.name: David
people.note: Shepherd, psalmist, and king of Israel.

people.name: Jonathan
people.note: Saul's son and David's closest friend.

people.name: Goliath
people.note: The Philistine champion David killed.

people.name: Bathsheba
people.note: Wife of Uriah, later of David, and mother of Solomon.

people.name: Absalom
people.note: David's son, who rebelled against him.

people.name: Solomon
people.note: David's son, who built the temple and was known for wisdom.

people.name: Elijah
people.note: Prophet who confronted Ahab and was taken up in a whirlwind.

people.name: Elias
people.note: The Greek form of Elijah, used in the New Testament.

people.name: Elisha
people.note: Elijah's successor as prophet.

people.name: Ahab
people.note: King of Israel, husband of Jezebel.

people.name: Jezebel
people.note: Ahab's queen, who promoted the worship of Baal.

people.name: Hezekiah
people.note: King of Judah who trusted God against Assyria.

people.name: Josiah
people.note: King of Judah who restored the law and the temple.

people.name: Isaiah
people.note: Prophet to Judah, who foretold the suffering servant.

people.name: Jeremiah
people.note: Prophet who warned Judah before the exile.

people.name: Ezekiel
people.note: Prophet among the exiles in Babylon.

people.name: Daniel
people.note: Taken to Babylon, where he served and prophesied.

people.name: Jonah
people.note: Sent to Nineveh, which he fled before going.

people.name: Nehemiah
people.note: Rebuilt the wall of Jerusalem after the exile.

people.name: Ezra
people.note: Priest and scribe who taught the law after the exile.

people.name: Esther
people.note: Queen of Persia who saved her people.

people.name: Mordecai
people.note: Esther's cousin, who raised her.

people.name: Job
people.note: A righteous man who lost everything and questioned God.

people.name: Jesus
people.note: The Christ, the Son of God.

people.name: Christ
people.note: The Greek rendering of Messiah, used as a title for Jesus.

people.name: Nicodemus
people.note: A Pharisee who came to Jesus by night.

people.name: Peter
people.note: The fisherman Simon, renamed Cephas, or Peter, meaning rock. A leader among the apostles, who denied Jesus and was restored.

people.name: Andrew
people.note: Peter's brother, one of the twelve.

people.name: Matthew
people.note: A tax collector called by Jesus, one of the twelve.

people.name: Thomas
people.note: One of the twelve, who doubted the resurrection until he saw.

people.name: Pilate
people.note: The Roman governor who handed Jesus over to be crucified.

people.name: Paul
people.note: Saul of Tarsus, a Pharisee who persecuted the church until Christ met him on the road to Damascus. Apostle to the Gentiles. Called Paul from Acts 13:9 onward.

people.name: Barnabas
people.note: Paul's companion on his first journey.

people.name: Silas
people.note: Paul's companion after Barnabas.

people.name: Timothy
people.note: Paul's younger fellow worker, who received two of his letters.

people.name: Titus
people.note: A Gentile co-worker of Paul, left in Crete.

people.name: Stephen
people.note: The first Christian martyr.

people.name: Lazarus
people.note: Brother of Mary and Martha, raised by Jesus.

people.name: Martha
people.note: Sister of Mary and Lazarus, of Bethany.

people.name: Zacchaeus
people.note: A chief tax collector of Jericho who climbed a tree to see Jesus.

places.name: Eden
places.note: The garden God planted, where Adam and Eve were placed.

places.name: Ararat
places.note: The mountains where the ark came to rest.

places.name: Babel
places.note: Where the tower was built and language was confused.

places.name: Ur
places.note: The city of the Chaldees that Abram's family left.

places.name: Haran
places.note: Where Abram's family settled before his call.

places.name: Canaan
places.note: The land promised to Abraham's descendants.

places.name: Shechem
places.note: Where God promised the land to Abram's seed.

places.name: Sichem
places.note: The older spelling of Shechem.

places.name: Bethel
places.note: Where Jacob dreamed of the ladder. Formerly called Luz.

places.name: Luz
places.note: The earlier name of Bethel.

places.name: Hebron
places.note: Where Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob were buried.

places.name: Sodom
places.note: A city of the plain, destroyed for its wickedness.

places.name: Gomorrah
places.note: Destroyed alongside Sodom.

places.name: Egypt
places.note: Where Israel was enslaved and from which they were delivered.

places.name: Goshen
places.note: The part of Egypt where Israel settled.

places.name: Sinai
places.note: The mountain where Moses received the law.

places.name: Horeb
places.note: Another name for the mountain of God.

places.name: Jordan
places.note: The river Israel crossed into the land, and where Jesus was baptised.

places.name: Jericho
places.note: The first city taken in Canaan, whose walls fell.

places.name: Gilgal
places.note: Israel's first camp after crossing the Jordan.

places.name: Shiloh
places.note: Where the tabernacle stood before the temple was built.

places.name: Bethlehem
places.note: The city of David, and the birthplace of Jesus.

places.name: Jerusalem
places.note: The city of David, where the temple stood.

places.name: Zion
places.note: The hill of Jerusalem, and a name for the city and its people.

places.name: Samaria
places.note: Capital of the northern kingdom, later the whole region.

places.name: Nazareth
places.note: Where Jesus grew up.

places.name: Capernaum
places.note: The town Jesus made the base of his Galilean ministry.

places.name: Galilee
places.note: The region where Jesus did much of his teaching.

places.name: Bethany
places.note: Home of Mary, Martha, and Lazarus.

places.name: Gethsemane
places.note: The garden where Jesus prayed before his arrest.

places.name: Golgotha
places.note: The place of a skull, where Jesus was crucified.

places.name: Calvary
places.note: The Latin-derived name for Golgotha.

places.name: Babylon
places.note: The empire that took Judah into exile.

places.name: Nineveh
places.note: The Assyrian capital Jonah was sent to.

places.name: Damascus
places.note: Where Saul was travelling when he met Christ.

places.name: Antioch
places.note: Where believers were first called Christians.

places.name: Tarsus
places.note: Paul's home city.

places.name: Ephesus
places.note: A city where Paul taught for some years.

places.name: Philippi
places.note: The first church Paul planted in Europe.

places.name: Corinth
places.note: A port city that received two of Paul's letters.

places.name: Athens
places.note: Where Paul preached at the Areopagus.

places.name: Rome
places.note: The capital of the empire, and where Paul was finally held.

places.name: Patmos
places.note: The island where John received the Revelation.

senses.note: Betrothed to Joseph, told by Gabriel that she would bear the Son of God. Present at the cross and with the disciples after the ascension.
Out of whom Jesus cast seven devils. She stood by the cross and was the first to see him risen.
Sister of Martha and Lazarus. She sat at Jesus' feet to listen, and anointed him before his burial.

senses.who: Mary the mother of James and Joses
senses.note: One of the women who watched the crucifixion and came to the tomb.

senses.who: Mary the mother of John Mark
senses.note: The believers met to pray in her house in Jerusalem.
Greeted by Paul as one who laboured much for the church there.
The fisherman Jesus renamed Cephas, or Peter, meaning rock. Called Simeon in Acts 15:14.
One of the twelve apostles, named in every list of them.
In whose house at Bethany Jesus was anointed.
Compelled to carry the cross of Jesus.
Who invited Jesus to eat, and judged the woman who anointed him.
Of Samaria, who tried to buy the gift of the Holy Ghost.
At whose house in Joppa Peter lodged.
Named among his brethren by those who knew the family.

senses.who: Saul, the first king of Israel
senses.note: Anointed by Samuel, he lost the kingdom through disobedience and died at Gilboa.
He held the coats at Stephen's death and persecuted the church, until Christ met him on the road to Damascus. Called Paul from Acts 13:9 onward.
Son of Zacharias and Elisabeth. He preached repentance, baptised Jesus, and was beheaded by Herod.
One of the twelve, brother of James, and the disciple Jesus loved. Traditionally the writer of the fourth Gospel, three letters, and the Revelation.
Who went with Barnabas and Paul, turned back at Perga, and was later useful to Paul again.
One of the twelve, brother of John, and the first apostle martyred, by Herod.
One of the twelve, named in every list of them.
A leader of the church at Jerusalem, who spoke at the council there.
One of the twelve, who betrayed Jesus for thirty pieces of silver.
Named among his brethren, and traditionally the writer of the letter of Jude.
One of the twelve, also called Thaddaeus, who asked how Jesus would show himself to them and not the world.
Sent with Silas from Jerusalem to carry the council's letter to Antioch.
Sold into Egypt by his brothers and raised to govern it, where he preserved his family through the famine.
A carpenter of Nazareth, of the house of David, who took Mary as his wife and raised Jesus.
A rich man and a disciple, who asked Pilate for the body of Jesus and laid it in his own tomb.
Surnamed Justus, and put forward with Matthias to replace Judas.
King of Judea at the birth of Jesus, who ordered the children of Bethlehem killed.
Tetrarch of Galilee, who beheaded John the Baptist and questioned Jesus before the crucifixion.
Who killed James with the sword, imprisoned Peter, and was struck down at Caesarea.
Before whom Paul made his defence, and who said he was almost persuaded.
One of the twelve, of Bethsaida, who brought Nathanael to Jesus.
One of the seven chosen to serve, who preached in Samaria and baptised the Ethiopian.
Brother of Herod Antipas, who ruled Ituraea and Trachonitis.

_ambiguous_note: Names borne by several different people. Each sense lists the books, and where it helps the chapter range, in which that person appears, so a verse can usually be matched to one of them. Where the scopes overlap or none match, the reader shows every possibility and says it is uncertain rather than choosing one.
